description: nf-core/proteinfold samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 2.0.0 schemas. Protein 3D structure prediction from one protein FASTA (D.PSEQ) per row.

mode.help: Prediction method, set from the question. Speed, a quick look, or many sequences: esmfold (a protein language model, no MSA and no database; least accurate, worst on orphan or designed proteins). Accuracy for a single chain or a complex: colabfold (AlphaFold2 weights with a fast MMseqs2 MSA) or alphafold2 (the reference method, slowest). A complex works in esmfold, colabfold and alphafold2 through their multimer presets. A ligand, cofactor, nucleic acid or modified residue needs an all-atom method (boltz, rosettafold_all_atom, alphafold3, helixfold3; rosettafold2na for protein-nucleic acid) AND a YAML or JSON input describing those molecules, which a D.PSEQ FASTA does not hold: such a question cannot be run from NExtSEEK today. Every mode but esmfold needs its database path (asked for before launch; none is staged on Luria). One mode per run. The fallback is esmfold, not upstream's default alphafold2, because alphafold2 with no staged database downloads about 2 TB into the run folder; esmfold downloads about 8 GB of weights.

esmfold_model_preset.help: ESMFold: multimer when the FASTA holds a complex (several chains to fold together: the D.PSEQ ChainCount is 2 or more, or the question asks about an interface or assembly); monomer for a single chain, or to fold several sequences one at a time. Set from ChainCount by the parameter atlas; upstream's default monomer is the fallback.

colabfold_model_preset.help: ColabFold: alphafold2_multimer_v3 when the FASTA holds a complex (ChainCount 2 or more, or an interface question); alphafold2_ptm for a single chain. Set from ChainCount by the parameter atlas; upstream's default alphafold2_ptm is the fallback.

alphafold2_model_preset.help: AlphaFold2: multimer when the FASTA holds a complex (ChainCount 2 or more, or an interface question); monomer_ptm for a single chain (it also reports pTM and PAE); monomer_casp14 when the question asks for the most accurate single-chain model and runtime does not matter (8x the ensembling). Set from ChainCount by the parameter atlas; upstream's default monomer_ptm is the fallback.

esmfold_num_recycles.help: ESMFold refinement passes. More (for example 8 to 12) for a hard target: a large or multi-domain protein, or one whose earlier model had low confidence. Upstream's default 4 is the fallback.

colabfold_num_recycles.help: ColabFold refinement passes. More (for example 6 to 12) for a hard target or a complex whose interface came out with low confidence. Upstream's default 3 is the fallback.

colabfold_use_amber.help: ColabFold: Amber relaxation of the models removes steric clashes, which docking or other physics-based use of the structure needs; false when only the fold or the confidence is wanted and speed matters. Upstream's default true is the fallback.

colabfold_use_templates.help: ColabFold: true when the question wants the model guided by known structures of close homologues (PDB templates); false for a de novo prediction. Upstream's default false is the fallback.

split_fasta.help: true when one FASTA holds several independent proteins to fold one by one (a list of variants or a family), not one complex; left unset (upstream's default) a multi-sequence FASTA is one entry, folded as a complex only with a multimer preset.

use_gpu.help: Run the predictors on a GPU. Not steerable: Luria GPU partitions are not confirmed and run.sh requests no GPU, so every run uses upstream's CPU default. ESMFold on CPU takes minutes per sequence; the MSA-based modes take far longer.

use_msa_server.help: Use the public ColabFold MMseqs2 server for MSAs instead of local databases. Not steerable: it sends the sequences to a server outside MIT, which needs the owner's ruling. Upstream's default (off, local databases) stands.

esmfold_db.help: Path on Luria to staged ESMFold weights (<path>/params/esmfold_3B_v1.pt and the two esm2 files). Not staged yet (not confirmed on Luria); left unset, each run downloads them (about 8 GB) into its DBs/ folder.

colabfold_db.help: colabfold mode only: path on Luria to the ColabFold databases (colabfold_envdb, colabfold_uniref30, params). Supplied by the user (see required_user_params); not staged on Luria.

alphafold2_db.help: alphafold2 mode only: path on Luria to the AlphaFold2 databases and parameters (about 2 TB). Supplied by the user (see required_user_params); not staged on Luria.

boltz_db.help: boltz mode only: path on Luria to the Boltz weights and CCD file. Supplied by the user (see required_user_params); not staged on Luria.

rosettafold_all_atom_db.help: rosettafold_all_atom mode only: path on Luria to its databases (UniRef30, BFD, PDB100) and weights. Supplied by the user (see required_user_params); not staged on Luria.

alphafold3_db.help: alphafold3 mode only: path on Luria to the AlphaFold3 databases. Supplied by the user (see required_user_params); not staged on Luria.

alphafold3_params_path.help: alphafold3 mode only: path on Luria to the AlphaFold3 model parameters, which Google releases only under its own licence and which cannot be downloaded by the pipeline. Supplied by the user (see required_user_params).

helixfold3_db.help: helixfold3 mode only: path on Luria to the HelixFold3 databases and weights. Supplied by the user (see required_user_params); not staged on Luria.

rosettafold2na_db.help: rosettafold2na mode only: path on Luria to the RoseTTAFold2NA databases and weights. Supplied by the user (see required_user_params); not staged on Luria.

multiqc_title.help: Title for the MultiQC report, when the user names the study.

pipeline.name: nf-core/proteinfold
pipeline.core_rule: Columns are id and fasta. fasta is required, with id or sequence beside it; Nessie writes id (the D.PSEQ UID). One protein or complex per row, one sequence per chain in its FASTA. The FASTA must be uncompressed (.fasta, .fa or .faa).
pipeline.reference_requirement: No genome. Each mode but esmfold needs its own database (ColabFold several hundred GB; AlphaFold2 about 2 TB; the all-atom modes similar), and none is staged on Luria: the path is asked for before launch. ESMFold downloads about 8 GB of weights per run unless esmfold_db names a staged copy. Luria GPU partitions are not confirmed, so runs are CPU-only.

validation_rules: The samplesheet must be a CSV named .csv (the input pattern is ^\S+\.csv$).
fasta must end .fasta, .fa or .faa; a gzipped FASTA is refused by the pinned schema.
A FASTA with several sequences is folded as ONE complex only with a multimer preset for the chosen mode; with split_fasta each sequence is folded on its own.
Every mode but esmfold needs its database path; never launch it without one, or the pipeline downloads the databases into the run folder.
Ligands, cofactors, nucleic acids and modified residues need a YAML or JSON input that NExtSEEK cannot build from a D.PSEQ FASTA: say so rather than folding the protein alone.
notes: NExtSEEK holds no D.PSEQ samples yet, and no assay produces them: the pipeline is catalogued so the capability exists when protein sequences are registered. Luria GPU partitions and the prediction databases are not confirmed; until they are, only esmfold runs without the user supplying a database path, and it runs on CPU.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/proteinfold input samplesheet.

id.description: Sequence name; names the output files.

fasta.description: The protein FASTA, one sequence per chain.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/proteinfold sheet from resolved D.PSEQ samples.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected when the user asks for the 3D structure of a protein or complex whose sequence is registered.
population_priority: One row per D.PSEQ leaf, id = its UID, fasta = its FASTA path.
Choose the mode from the question (speed vs accuracy, single chain vs complex) and the preset from ChainCount.
final_checks: A non-esmfold mode carries its database path.

runtime.basis: First guess for ESMFold on one 16-CPU Luria node with no GPU (Nessie's default submit); not measured on Luria. Setup is the ~8 GB weight download when esmfold_db is unset. The MSA-based modes take far longer on CPU (hours per sequence) and are not covered by these numbers. Refine from real runs.
